title.narrative: Output 5.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative:
Knowledge on arrangements to enhance industry participation in the development or enhancement of competency standards have been introduced to constituents.
These arrangements on competency standards development are expected to complement TESDA’s thrust to actively engage industry boards and similar mechanisms in the review or development of competency standards, curriculum, training delivery, assessment and certification. With support from the Government of United Kingdom, the ILO conducted the Review of Practices and Policy Options for the Development of Competency Standards, Qualifications, and Curricula: Case Study of Scotland, Singapore, and New Zealand. A related review of national practices on competency standards development was also produced.
Using the information in the review report, the ILO convened a knowledge exchange forum which convened 80 representatives from industry, government, TVET institutions and the academe in discussions on ways to improve the process of competency standards development so the same expeditiously responds to ever-changing industry skills needs.

title.narrative: 5.2.2. Number of Member States with inclusive skills and lifelong learning governance models
Output 5.1. Increased capacity of Member States to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative:
TVET planners and administrators particularly from TESDA, DOLE, Public Employment Service Offices (PESOs), industry organizations and TVET institutions, at both the national and regional levels, have improved capacity to anticipate future skills needs based on labour market demands. This improved knowledge on an analytical approach on using the country’s labour force survey (LFS) to analyse demand for and supply of skilled workforce at the regional/sub-national level contributed to TESDA’s thrust for area-based demand driven TVET planning and delivery.
Further, in-depth capacity building on the fundamentals of labour market information and TVET statistics strengthened the capacity of TESDA planning focal persons in the country’s 16 regions in formulating skills priorities plans as basis for TVET planning and delivery, particularly the regional allocation of scholarship slots.
In Region 7 (Central Visayas), stakeholders in the construction sector identified and anticipated skills needs in the construction sector using the Skills for Trade and Economic Diversification (STED) methodology. This enhanced sectoral capacity contributed not only to regional implementation of area-based demand-driven TVET planning and delivery but also boosted the capacity of the regional construction industry board Cebu Contractors Association (CCA) in anticipating demand for skilled workforce in the sector​ With support from the Government of United Kingdom, the ILO introduced an LFS-based methodology for analysing demand for and supply of skilled workforce which was piloted in the Visayas regions. The pilot implementation produced 3 region-specific analyses of demand for skilled labour; 2 reports documenting data on TVET providers and jobseekers in the Visayas regions; a manual on the analysis of demand for labour and its application to TVET delivery and planning in the Philippines; and a training guide on the fundamentals of labour market information and TVET statistics for TVET planning and delivery. The manual is referred to by TESDA as it implements reforms in collecting and analysing labour market information as basis for TVET planning and delivery.
The ILO also supported the training of 495 individuals on using the LFS-based methodology for measuring demand for and supply of skilled workforce; 30 stakeholders in Region 7 were introduced to the STED approach to determine the demand for skilled workers in the construction sector while 40 TESDA and DOLE Planning Focal persons were trained on the fundamentals of labour market information as used for TVET planning and delivery.​

With support from the Government of United Kingdom, the ILO supported the development of a manual on the analysis of demand for labour and its application to TVET delivery and planning in the Philippines. This Manual is referred by the TESDA Planning Office LMI Division as it implements reforms in collecting and analysing labour market information as basis for TVET planning and delivery.

title.narrative: 5.1.2. Number of Member States with institutionalized national or sectoral mechanisms to measure skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs
Output 5.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative:
The government, with social partners and other stakeholders piloted an inclusive, area-based and sector-specific lifelong learning model in the Visayas regions. The model has been recognized by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) as basis for formulating legislation aimed at reforming the Philippine education sector. The intention to strengthen skills development and Lifelong learning is reflected in the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028, the Labor and Employment Plan 2023-2028 and the National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan 2023-2028.
Through pilot implementation of approaches that underscored multi-stakeholder partnerships for the delivery of skills upgrading; targeting of specific vulnerable and marginalized groups; sector-based competency standards and curriculum development, skills training delivery and vocational guidance and counselling; and, promotion of public-private partnerships, the approaches are expected to be sustained through local ordinances and partnership agreements in each of the localities where the pilots were implemented. With support from the Government of United Kingdom, the ILO undertook several reviews as basis for the pilot implementation of lifelong learning approaches. These assessments or reviews focused on: 1) national policies and programmes on lifelong learning; initiatives on recognition of prior learning (RPL) in TESDA; practices on public-private financing of inclusive skills development and lifelong learning; and a market assessment on career guidance for youth in the Philippines.
The ILO also provided support in the pilot implementation of inclusive, area-based and sector -specific approaches in four localities in the Visayas regions, namely: Tubungan and Libacao in Region 6; the cities of Cebu, Mandaue and Lapu-lapu in Region 7 and Basey in Region 8. These pilots demonstrated targeted skills training delivery; strengthened linkages between various pathways for recognizing skills such as TVET, alternative learning systems (ALS), and recognition of prior learning (RPL). It also modelled sector-specific vocational guidance; initiatives on support or auxiliary services to complement skills upgrading; and multi-stakeholder coordination in implementing the approaches.
Support from the ILO for these pilots also covered the development of new competency standards in economic sectors identified to create better employment and income opportunities for vulnerable and marginalized groups. These are in tikog and buri production and processing in Basey, Region 8 and abaca-grading in Libacao, Region 6.
